June 2017

June 16, 2017

We've taken so many cute photos here and it seems inappropriate to flood Facebook with them but couldn't resist posting a few from today. Love how even the commute to do fun stuff is fun in itself- we took a river boat and a motorbike to get here, then a sky train and a regular train to get back ☺️ and if you haven't noticed by now, we love pools of all kinds- water, sprinkles, balls, you name it. 👌🏻

June 30, 2017Luang Prabang, Laos

#1 rated restaurant in LPB, and extra bonus they have ice cream for the kids while I drink my organic locally sourced latte 😂 I've had people from all over the world ask me who I'm traveling with and be shocked that I'm by myself with two kids. "How do you do it???" I have no idea, some days they drive me crazy, but it's funny that two kids are difficult, no matter what culture you come from.
PS- we really love Laos!

September 2017

September 12, 2017

Recent photos of the kids. They are alive and thriving. The international school I want to put them in is full for the year so instead, they're doing activities and a bit of world schooling which is ideal since we travel frequently. I'd argue that they are learning as much if not more than they would in preschool:

They learned a bit about gravity and physics by throwing rocks, both big and small, into the Laotian section of the Mekong river.

They’re identifying and trying new fruits: they particularly like dragonfruit, mangosteen, and starfruit. Ella even tried some durian.

We learned the Mekong river basin is home to some of the largest biodiversity in the world, second only to the amazon

We have tried all forms of transport: tuk tuk, truck back, sky train, underground train, minibus, motorbike, all sorts of boats and ferries, regular bus, plane, and of course cars. They’re seasoned travelers and quite easy to bring around.

We got to bathe and walk elephants, hear gibbons sing, Ella snorkeled and saw fish in the ocean for the first time, a wild pack of monkeys stole bananas from their hands and grabbed Ella by her dress.

They’re learning about different languages, and regularly greet Thai in the traditional way. They speak some common Thai words we hear with a humorously accurate accent.

They've watched me bargain with vendors and are very good at walking away from things that they really want because they understand there will be more vendors with the same items and we want to buy from a nice person at a good price.

We talk about the value of items and that some things may be cheap, but they are not good quality. They've seen poor quality toys break after minimal use, and that often we would rather buy better quality things for more.

They've found all kinds of beautiful shells on the beaches out there, and have built up quite a collection. We've also seen hermit crabs, frogs, giant lizards, exotic birds, butterflies in all colors, and a myriad of other animals in their natural habitat.

They know the difference between wild animals and pets, and know not to touch the street cats & dogs. We've made some exceptions for puppies.

Winston's exceptionally good at recognizing places we've walked by, such as random restaurants or where we got dropped off. He loves reading maps and often times direct us to places he’s been to.

They often pay for their own treats and get the change, we're learning the worth of different bills and coins. Soon I'll give them an allowance to spend as they wish so they can start managing money and decide for themselves if they want to buy something and if it's worth it.

They're learning the names of the MRT stops we go to often, can recognize the names when they're announced, and try to recognize what gates we are at, or what number our room is etc.

They swim almost every day, and we often go on walks to get my morning coffee or to grab lunch. We always discover new things along the way. Winston said he "loves long belaxing walks". Ella has learned how to swim!

They've learned there are good and bad people. We have had one bad experience with someone, but majority of the people we have encountered we've had overwhelmingly positive experiences with. Most of the people here love kids and I like seeing the joy that the kids bring to others. People often follow them and take photos of them and are very helpful.

They each have a backpack that they pack themselves for trips. They're responsible for remembering what to bring, and keeping track of their belongings.

Motor skills- when we got here, Ella couldn't get onto an escalator by herself. Now she can and she's so proud of herself. Winston can open and close various locks (after locking us out w the chain lock at home and not being able to open it!)

Just about the only thing they miss from California is Disneyland. Ella sometimes asks “Can we go to Disneyland today?” I haven’t had the heart to tell them there is no Disneyland here…. However, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai and even Paris is just a flight away and I’m sure we’ll make our way to all of them.

So relax, Mom. Kids are doing great!

September 27, 2017Siem Reap, Cambodia

Though she be but little, she is fierce - W.S.
Every time I look at her lately, I am in awe of how quickly she is growing so I thought we'd spend some one on one time together. Ella loves temples so we got on a flight to Siem Reap in Cambodia to explore the ruins of Angkor for a few days. It's quite incredible here- deemed one of the seven wonders of the world, and appropriately so.
My little adventurer.

February 2018

February 23, 2018

A little update on the kids

Winston started international school here in Bangkok last semester and I was initially really reluctant to put him in it because it's a very academic school which we are not used to as in the US he wouldn't even be in Kindergarten right now, but I'm so happy with the progress he's made. He is able to write and recognize all his letters, starting to read, and learning numbers and addition/subtraction. He has been writing letters for his friends on his own, and has really gotten into drawing. They draw and paint almost every day and I love seeing their creations and creativity.

Outside of school, they are exposed to various activities, having just finished playdoh & cooking courses. We regularly make playdoh at home and they help me with cooking and baking. They've both learned how to swim and we try to go to the beach cities often. They love legos and have really gotten creative making their own things, and also following instructions for sets. We also love playing music and dancing at home.

Ella recently enjoyed body surfing at the beach, while Winston caught a crab and learned how to jump over waves. Winston has always been more reserved but he's really come out of his shell and talking and interacting with people we meet on our travels. He likes the friends he has made at school.

Winston recently saw the "long neck" women in a video and was really curious about them, so he was excited to be able to actually meet some and interact with them in person in Burma. Ella loves exploring temples so she went with me to see Angkor Wat in Cambodia. They have videos put together of their travels on their ipads so they can remember them, and they love to watch them. I'm also finishing up a photobook of the last year for them to look through.

They enjoy the little parts of our daily routine, buying fruits from the fruit stand, taking tuk tuk rides home, going to the farmers markets, bus rides to other cities, saying hello in thai to the staff in

I’m more proud of my son putting together his own legos than anything I’ve done in my entire life 😂. I used to have to guide him on which step to do next but now that he’s learned to read numbers he did a 68 piece set on his own! 😍

September 6, 2018Bangkok, Thailand

One of the best parts of living in a big city is how condensed everything is. There’s much more of a neighborhood feel. The kids start seeing people they know from the moment they leave the house and get greeted everywhere, it’s wonderful. They’re greeted by the lobby staff, the drivers outside, various street vendors, and they run into their school friends everywhere, some of whom live in the same condo. So many neighbors to play with! It’s a great part of our routine. We never got this feeling in LA as we didn’t live in buildings and the homes are very spread out and everyone lived far away from each other and, at least where we lived, everyone kept to themselves. In general, Thais love kids and are very friendly to them. 😊😊😊

December 29, 2018from Ayutthaya, Thailand

This morning started with a history lesson that tied some of our travels together. Woke up to a pink sky overlooking temples and a river in the city of Ayutthaya, also known as Ancient Siam. My conversation with the kids went like this:
Today we are going to tour Ayutthaya. Ayutthaya was once the center of Thailand where many people lived, including kings. It was where everything happened until the Burmese came and destroyed the city and took all the gold. The temples here used to be covered in gold, but when the Burmese attacked the city, they took all the gold back to their country. Do you remember when we went all around Myanmar and saw the beautiful golden temple in Yangon? The gold to make the Shwedagon came from Ayutthaya. After the city was destroyed, the center of Thailand moved to Bangkok, where we now live. Today we’ll explore what is left of this city.
I’m not much of a history buff but I definitely would have paid more attention in school if I actually got to see the places I learned about. So cool to build upon their knowledge with real experiences. Tomorrow we’re off to a floating market and the famous Thai train market. School breaks out here are 🔥🔥

May 30, 2021Trader Joe's- Madison,WI

Winston and Ella started their first “business” selling plants. They’ve made just under $50 so far and got experience talking to their customers. Now, they each got to spend $5 of their money to buy anything they want at Trader Joe’s incorporating math skills and learning to budget 😋

May 30, 2021Verona, Wisconsin

Kids new passports came in, the result of a hard earned battle. You need both parents’ permission to renew minor passports. Their father refused to renew it even during the start of the pandemic leaving us essentially stuck in Thailand. I had to petition with the US Embassy and work with their lawyers in DC to have emergency 1 year passports issued to allow us to move back to the US. That year was about to expire and we were automatically granted permission to turn them into new full 5 year passports good until 2026 💪🏻

Now in Wisconsin there is binding case law stating that unreasonable refusal to renew minor passports result in legal custody given to the asking party. This will hold them over til they turn 18 and no longer need permission for passports.

The law is power.

October 2, 2021

I’ve had a tough month!
A few weeks ago, I almost died. It was the closest to death I’ve ever been in my life (and I’ve done some pretty stupid things).
Then, Ella got Covid. Then Winston, and now I have it too. Even though I’m fully vaccinated and have a “mild” case, it still feels like one of the worst illnesses I’ve ever had.
Last weekend I started feeling a little sick, and by Monday I was bedridden. Cold chills and fevers through Wednesday and could not get out of bed. By Thursday I was able to get up and walk around, and then yesterday, Friday, I lost all sense of taste and smell. I’m ALOT better but still have a sore throat and sometimes struggle to breathe.
Oh, and then two days ago my basement flooded lol.

December 31, 2021Grain Bin Commoditiesvideo

We just got back from our first long camper trip.
Wisconsin > Pittsburgh > Philadelphia > DC > Virginia > Tennesee > Wisconsin
~3000 miles
The kids got to do SO many things. Some highlights include:
A ton of museums along the way including the Spy Museum in DC
Stayed at several farms and even “worked” on some of them
Explored a 2 mile long cave where the only light came from our helmets and there were very tight spaces to crawl through. We were also the only ones allowed to camp outside of the cave that night
Woke up at the top of a mountain winery where we were once again their only guest
Milked a goat on Cassandra Morgan Beiling’s farm!
Saw so many stars, conveniently right after we got some stargazing lessons at the Pittsburgh planetarium.
Lots and lots of closeup animal encounters.
Made tons of friends and saw sights off the beaten path.
I’m quite certain that this camper is the best purchase I have ever made.

January 23, 2022

Kids and I went on our first guided mushroom tour today (yes in winter!). It was so much fun and the kids wanted to share a summary of what they learned.

We picked up mushroom foraging as a hobby last year and found fun shrooms like chicken of the woods, giant puffballs, and wild oyster mushrooms. All of which are edible and SO yummy!

Thank you to Tavis Lynch for inviting us to this foray with the Wisconsin Mycological Society. Tavis is a leading expert in mushroom...ology and it was amazing learning from him and other board members of the WMS 🙂

We'll be ordering some of Tavis's Mushrooms mushroom kits to grow mushrooms at home while we wait for the weather to warm up.

Can't wait to apply what we learned today to find morels next! 🥰

January 30, 2022

Another week, another fun winter activity 🙂. I'd actually been wanting to do this for a while so it was a treat to get the real Midwestern experience and go ICE FISHING! Both kids caught a fish and they were super proud of themselves.
Thank you for the invite Nathaniel Hope. The Yahara Fishing Club gifted each of the kids all the supplies they needed, hot dogs, hot chocolate, and a lesson on how to ice fish! Ella & Winston had a crew of expert fishermen teaching them what to do. They did an amazing job. 🥰
Fun background story:
I'd been wanting to move back to the US but didn't know exactly where I wanted to be. I didn't want to be in a crowded city after living in Bangkok. I had a list of preferences I wanted in a city which I discussed with a Wisconsin lawyer Jake Skebba who was in Thailand. He told me Madison sounded like it was what I was looking for. Initially, I was like Wisconsin? What is that...? Where is it?? Who goes there? (lol). However, I respect Jake's opinion so I researched further on Madison even though we had never been before.
Madison was already sounding like it met all the requirements that I wanted in a city: lots of nature, no traffic, ability to bike, lake life, clean streets, clean air, low crime, short commutes, good education, etc.
When told I was thinking about moving to Wisconsin, a friend in Thailand James Martin connected me with Nathaniel who made me aware that a Mandarin Immersion school existed here. The school is what sealed the deal. Hence... we live the life we live today in large part because of James, Nathaniel, and Jake.
Funny how little connections make big differences

September 24, 2022Skelly's Farm Market

Fall is here which means time for farm activities!
By far our favorite farm that we’ve been to in Wisconsin is Skelly’s which has free admission, ridiculously delicious apple cider donuts made fresh (along with other treats that sell out), fun playground, and a lot of other activities on top of your usual corn maze and pumpkin patches.
A close second is Enchanted Acres which has a super long slide and lots of activities. It’s also closer to Madison.
We found Sutter Ridge underwhelming with cold donuts and unwelcoming “don’t steal the honey crisps” signs everywhere. They do have a reasonable max price on pumpkins which is nice because last year we got an almost $100 pumpkin at Skelly’s.
(This post is more for my own reference than anything else since I can never remember the name of the farms )

A couple times a year I’ll ask my kids to gather all their pants with holes in it so that I can throw them away. We just did this recently. Winston is not a fan of this and insists that his pants are perfectly fine and that I just sew up any holes so he can continue wearing them. I don’t let him do that.
This morning he asks, “Why do your pants have holes in it?”
“It’s the style”, I replied.
“How come when YOUR pants have holes in it it’s ‘style’ but when mine have holes you make me throw it away?”
good point, kiddo. (my pants are jeans and theirs are soft fabric-y material. )
My daughter then chimes in, “are you sure it’s supposed to be like that? That’s a big hole”
“Well there used to be threads that ran across but they broke”
“Because your knees are too fat?” she asks.
they make good points and crack me up. Perhaps it’s time to retire these jeans

January 15, 2023

Milwaukee is Wisconsin’s largest city, it’s an hour away from Madison and twice as big (in terms of population). The overall feel of the downtown area reminds me of a mini Chicago. We’ve been a few times but not even close to thoroughly exploring it.
Winston’s been into magic lately and there happened to be a magic show touring in Milwaukee so I decided to make a day trip out of it today.
We arrived early and went to a children’s museum first, Discovery World— beautifully located right on Lake Michigan. It’s a small but high tech science museum with a similarly small but impressive aquarium. The kids got to play with electricity, pet sturgeons and sting rays, and see live axolotl.
Milwaukee doesn’t have *alot* of museums but the museums that it does have are pretty great. I LOVE the Public Museum and would recommend it to anyone visiting MKE. I’ve never been able to make it through the entire building in one trip, and try to go as often as possible since it is shutting down in a couple years (technically moving but the new location is not going to be the same at all).
For lunch we had Cuban food and it was beyond delicious. We tried a sampler plate of plantains cooked 3 different ways and the usual Cuban dishes. The kids devoured their food.
Our show started at 2:30 and it was our first time in the Milwaukee theatre. I booked this thinking it would be just something the kids would enjoy but it turned out to be one of the best shows we have ever watched, it blew our minds! There was a standing ovation from the crowd and the kids gushed about the magic for hours afterwards. I have never heard them gush about anything and they’ve seen lots of cool things. I highly recommend Champions of Magic if it’s showing near you.
For dinner we all had Ethiopian food for the first time. I have no point of reference but it seemed pretty authentic and we had a great experience. Guests don’t eat on regular tables but on an elevated woven basket like thing and with bare hands. We read about the country of Ethiopia while we waited for our food. I was vigilant about hand washing since I knew we were about to eat without utensils . The food was yummy, I was happy that both of them eagerly tried all of the different samples even though they’d never seen it before. We enjoyed all the new flavors. This particular place (Ethiopian Cottage Village) is consistently rated as a top MKE restaurant and people apparently drive for hours to dine here so I’m glad it was mere minutes away from the theatre.
All in all, a very satisfying cultural day, or as the kids kept saying, “very entertaining!”.
Visit Milwaukee if you ever get the chance, with or without kids

February 20, 2023

The kids spent the summer in LA and Hawaii, and in the last few months were in NYC, Philly, and Chicago twice. I find it amusing that though they like our trips and the amenities in the larger metros, whenever we’re headed home they always mention that Madison is so much nicer and they love Wisconsin.
According to them, big cities are loud and dirty, the people are rude, and there’s too much honking
One of the questions I get asked most is if I am happy with my decision to move here and overall I would say yes. It is a great place for kids. Would I live here by myself? No lol. Would I visit in the summer? Absolutely haha.
Wisconsin in the summer is one of the best places on earth we missed it last year so this year I’m intent on staying around, and everyone is welcome to visit

IMO though, travel is the best education. Nothing like some real life experience.
We made a quick stop in Qatar where they rode camels in the famed Arabian market and had some real middle eastern food (the best hummus we’ve ever had).
Landed in HCM and explored the late night walking streets and had some pho at 4 in the morning. After a few days we flew to the northern islands where we stayed at the most beautiful ocean view resort and took a cruise to see the hundreds of limestone islands and kayaked to private beaches.
When we returned to civilzation in Hanoi, we got some blank journals and they’re required to keep a book of their travels. They have identified the names, flags, and locations of the countries of South East Asia. Every day they write an entry on what they did and their observation of the different landscapes they have seen.
They grew up in this environment but it’s been 3 years since we left the US. Now they’re older and able to think on a higher level and have a better understanding. They’re using their phones to navigate us through the chaotic streets. They calculate the exchange rates and learn the value of money. They see the cultural differences in each place we go and are learning to traverse through the motorbike filled streets of VN.
They see everything from high end hotels to remote fishing villages of varying construct. The disparity of living between the privileged and those less so. It helps a person to not take things for granted, I think. I told my son there is very little difference between the foreigner on vacation, and the ones working in the village-- merely the luck of being born into more privileged circumstances. If you are lucky enough to have an education, use it to make the world a better place.
In school they had units on country life v city life, on countries, math, science, humanities, history etc. Now, we live it
Missed this life quite a bit and glad to be back, if only for a while.

May 5, 2023

Educational diaries:

Traditional schooling has its benefits, for sure, but education is everywhere. I have no idea if we’re following the regular US curriculum (probably not) but in just the last few weeks:

An NYU dental surgeon joined us for part of our trip. Winston and Ella got detailed lessons on teeth, and the formation of cavities. We all changed our tooth brushing routine as well.

We met one of my best friends, CEO of an international company, in a few different cities and they got lessons on energy and business. We toured their new HCM office and the kids found it amusing that they had offices in every country we were in during our trip. They asked about hiring and firing, and listened to our discussions on some of the problems encountered in every day work life.

After reading about the Khmer Kingdom and the world wonder of Angkor Wat we toured it in person and marveled at the carvings and engineering— which would be hard to replicate even with modern technology and lasers.

On our way to the airport to go to Taiwan we had an in depth conversation about Ed Sheeran and his copyright trial. I broke down the main arguments of each side and the ramifications of the decision should the plaintiff win. They learned a little about the idea of “precedent” in American law. Both expressed interest in watching the trial.

We met with a friend who owns a wealth management company and he gave the kids a lesson on probability and strategy while we played board games.

I’ve watched them grow in confidence and independence as they venture on their own in our old neighborhood, picking up food or other little errands. They are comfortable speaking to adults, expressing their needs to staff, or even standing up for themselves or other kids when necessary (to the dismay of our friends’ nanny I’m sure ).

They are reconnecting with their childhood friends and meeting a lot of new friends, all of whom come from very diverse backgrounds, all different countries. It’s delightful that no matter how different the kids can be, play and joy are universal.

They also spend time with lots of adults (mom’s friends) and recognize how many people have gone out of their way to welcome us and meet with us. They’ve loved seeing people they remember, many who we’ve gone on incredible trips with and are forever a part of their childhood memories.

We’ve been through many airports on this trip and I’ve tasked them with navigating us through by themselves from check in, through security, and to find our gate. They’ve learned about immigration, visas, and passports.

Winston has grown very interested in business, the concept of money, and regularly gives his thoughts on how a business is run or what makes one business do better than another, or how they might possibly improve.

At breakfast this morning Ella brought up the various traits of each country she’s been to and they’re both keenly aware that every place has its pros and cons.

They have very interesting, and often accurate, insight on human behavior, personalities, and motivation.

Between all this, they’re also doing weekly reading and math, mostly books through Libby and practice on Khan Academy. They’ve also kept up with their travel journal, which is almost full and definitely a keepsake that they’ve worked hard on and are very proud of.

The substantive facts they are learning (like all the countries in SEA or the history of a place) I often did not know myself until I either looked it up so I could teach them or were taught by friends who specialize in the matter.

The soft skills they’re acquiring at a young age are, in my opinion, the truly invaluable part of this experience.

It’s often said that parenting is a thankless job but I have found that to be anything but true. My kids regularly express without prompting how grateful they are. For the food we get to have, the experiences, the gifts, for the fun with friends. It makes my heart full

I had an internal struggle for months on whether or not to go on this trip and can say with confidence that it was absolutely the best decision

Next week Ella turns 9 and their childhood will be half over. I hope they take their unique upbringing and choose to lead interesting and fulfilling lives, anywhere in the world.

December 9, 2023Sa Pa, Vietnam

Oh, the places you’ll go
This year we made some big changes. After years of deliberation I finally pulled the kids out of traditional school and put them into virtual school, officially untethering us from a single location.
It’s something I thought about for years but was nervous about since it’s not the norm for childhood education. However it’s been working out great, even better than we could have hoped. My kids constantly exclaim that they’re learning so much and I can see it too.
I’m working remotely, the kids study 4-5 hours a day and they’re learning important life skills like time management, independence, computer skills (typing, document storing/uploading, internet navigation, research)... I am more involved with their education on a day-to-day basis, and they are getting real life experience too.
Just had a big birthday pass and while life is unexpected, it has been full, fulfilling, filled with family, food, fun, adventures, and love I couldn’t ask for more (except maybe a bathtub in our current rental )
